task.title: Causal idempotent inbox
task.specification: config={} . Every event is {id:string,seq:positive integer,delta:integer}. The inbox starts value=0,next=1. First-seen IDs with a free sequence at or above next are recorded permanently for this instance. Reuse of an ID with exactly its original seq/delta is duplicate; changed reuse is conflict. A new ID at a sequence already reserved is conflict, and a new ID below next is stale. Otherwise status=accepted; immediately apply every consecutively available sequence beginning at next, adding its delta exactly once. Output {status,value,next,pending}, where pending is ascending unapplied sequence numbers. Deduplication covers the complete instance, including applied operations; there is no time-based cleanup. Return one JSON output per event; state is opaque JSON, initially null. Objects in outputs have exactly the documented keys; map keys are unordered, arrays are ordered. Sorted/lexicographic string order compares Unicode scalar values (code points), with a shorter prefix first. Numeric inputs/values and intermediate arithmetic are safe integers. Integral JSON number notations such as 1 and 1.0 denote the same number, while booleans are distinct. Strings contain Unicode scalar values (no unpaired surrogates). Decoded imported values outside these limits are invalid frames. There are at most 48 events. Unknown/invalid operations have the behavior below. Each instance starts fresh. Hidden ordinary cases vary legal values; boundary cases emphasize equality, empty data and duplicates; adversarial cases reorder and conflict; shift cases use longer traces and more identities within the same contract.

matchedCard.label: Dendrochronology
matchedCard.relation: Overlapping sequences can be aligned by distinctive patterns spanning several observations. Cross-comparison can reveal missing or extra local observations that a simple position count would treat as elapsed intervals.
assumptions: The sequences share a comparable underlying history.
The overlap contains enough distinguishing structure to support alignment.
matchedCard.boundary: Repeated patterns or insufficient overlap can support several alignments. A single coincident observation does not establish a unique chronological match.
matchedCard.source_fact: NOAA describes crossdating tree-ring patterns from several trees to account for missing or extra rings and align samples from different periods.

shuffledCard.label: Comparator hysteresis
shuffledCard.relation: A state-dependent comparator uses distinct upper and lower transition thresholds. Between them, the existing state is retained. Fluctuations that remain within this interval need not cause repeated switching.
assumptions: The output has a preceding state.
Distinct thresholds are appropriate to the signal range and acceptable response delay.
shuffledCard.boundary: A wider separation can postpone response to a real change. Behavior with two state-dependent thresholds differs from reacting to every crossing of one fixed threshold.
shuffledCard.source_fact: Texas Instruments describes an inverting comparator with upper and lower hysteresis thresholds to reduce unwanted transitions caused by noise or slow-moving signals.

initial.explanation: Maintain permanent ID records and unique sequence reservations. Existing IDs are duplicate only when both original fields match; otherwise conflict. New IDs below next are stale, while sequences already reserved conflict. Accepted records are repeatedly applied in sequence order from next.
initial.mapping: state.n is the next unapplied sequence, state.v is accumulated value, and state.a stores permanent [id,seq,delta] records. Reservations include applied records. Each output reports status, current value, next, and sorted pending sequences.
initial.assumptions: Inputs follow the stated event contract and use safe integers. The implementation treats malformed events defensively as conflicts, although legal traces contain only valid events.
initial.holds: (input,out)=>{if(!Array.isArray(out)||out.length!==input.events.length)return false;let n=1,v=0,a=[];for(let k=0;k<input.events.length;k++){let e=input.events[k],s='accepted',old=a.find(x=>x[0]===e.id);if(old)s=old[1]===e.seq&&old[2]===e.delta?'duplicate':'conflict';else if(e.seq<n)s='stale';else if(a.some(x=>x[1]===e.seq))s='conflict';else a.push([e.id,e.seq,e.delta]);if(s==='accepted')for(;;){let x=a.find(x=>x[1]===n);if(!x)break;v+=x[2];n++}let p=a.filter(x=>x[1]>=n).map(x=>x[1]).sort((x,y)=>x-y),q=out[k];if(!q||Object.keys(q).length!==4||q.status!==s||q.value!==v||q.next!==n||JSON.stringify(q.pending)!==JSON.stringify(p))return false}return true}

final.explanation: The implementation keeps permanent records for every accepted ID and sequence. Existing IDs are duplicates only when both sequence and delta match; otherwise they conflict. A new ID conflicts if its sequence is already reserved, is stale if it is below the next unapplied sequence, and is accepted otherwise. After acceptance, all contiguous reserved sequences are applied exactly once. Pending sequences remain sorted and exclude applied entries.

initial.explanation: Track every accepted identity and sequence permanently. New events are rejected as stale or conflicting before insertion; accepted events are inserted, then contiguous pending sequences are applied exactly once.
initial.mapping: state.n is the next unapplied sequence, state.v is the accumulated value, state.i maps IDs to [seq,delta], and state.q maps reserved sequence numbers to [delta].
initial.assumptions: Events satisfy the stated legal input constraints. State is returned only to the same instance and is not externally modified.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;var n=1,v=0,ids={},qs={};for(var k=0;k<input.events.length;k++){var e=input.events[k],s=e.seq,id=e.id,d=e.delta,status;if(ids[id])status=ids[id][1]===d?'duplicate':'conflict';else if(qs[s]!==undefined)status='conflict';else if(s<n)status='stale';else{ids[id]=[s,d];qs[s]=d;status='accepted';while(qs[n]!==undefined){v+=qs[n];n++}}var p=[];for(var x in qs)if(+x>=n)p.push(+x);p.sort(function(a,b){return a-b});var o=output[k];if(!o||o.status!==status||o.value!==v||o.next!==n||JSON.stringify(o.pending)!==JSON.stringify(p))return false}return true}

final.explanation: The implementation keeps permanent identity records and sequence reservations in arrays, avoiding key-collision behavior for arbitrary legal strings. Each event is classified before mutation. Accepted reservations are then applied in contiguous sequence order exactly once, while pending reservations are returned numerically sorted.

initial.explanation: A causal inbox reserves each accepted sequence permanently, applies contiguous sequences once, and retains identity records for idempotent duplicate/conflict detection.
initial.mapping: The inbox value is the accumulated delta of applied sequence records; next is the first unapplied sequence; pending contains reserved unapplied sequences; identity records provide permanent deduplication.
initial.assumptions: New IDs below next are stale before sequence-reservation checks. Existing IDs are classified as duplicate only when both sequence and delta match; otherwise they conflict.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!applies(input)||!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;let r={v:0,n:1,a:[]};for(let i=0;i<input.events.length;i++){let e=input.events[i],status='accepted',old=null;for(let x of r.a)if(x[0]===e.id){old=x;break}if(old){status=old[1]===e.seq&&old[2]===e.delta?'duplicate':'conflict'}else if(e.seq<r.n)status='stale';else{for(let x of r.a)if(x[1]===e.seq){status='conflict';break}if(status==='accepted')r.a.push([e.id,e.seq,e.delta])}if(status==='accepted'){for(;;){let k=-1;for(let j=0;j<r.a.length;j++)if(r.a[j][1]===r.n){k=j;break}if(k<0)break;r.v+=r.a[k][2];r.n++}}let p=[];for(let x of r.a)if(x[1]>=r.n)p.push(x[1]);p.sort((a,b)=>a-b);let z=output[i];if(!z||z.status!==status||z.value!==r.v||z.next!==r.n||JSON.stringify(z.pending)!==JSON.stringify(p))return false}return true}
initial.program: function solve({config,state,event}){let s=state||{v:0,n:1,a:[]},e=event,status='accepted',old=null;for(let x of s.a)if(x[0]===e.id){old=x;break}if(old)status=old[1]===e.seq&&old[2]===e.delta?'duplicate':'conflict';else if(e.seq<s.n)status='stale';else{for(let x of s.a)if(x[1]===e.seq){status='conflict';break}if(status==='accepted')s.a.push([e.id,e.seq,e.delta])}if(status==='accepted'){for(;;){let k=-1;for(let i=0;i<s.a.length;i++)if(s.a[i][1]===s.n){k=i;break}if(k<0)break;s.v+=s.a[k][2];s.n++}}let p=[];for(let x of s.a)if(x[1]>=s.n)p.push(x[1]);p.sort((a,b)=>a-b);return{state:s,output:{status:status,value:s.v,next:s.n,pending:p}}}

final.explanation: Maintains permanent identity records as [id, sequence, delta], plus the accumulated value and next unapplied sequence. Existing IDs are duplicates only when both sequence and delta match; otherwise conflicts. New IDs below next are stale, while sequences already reserved by another ID conflict. Accepted records are inserted, then all contiguous sequences from next are applied exactly once. Pending sequences are emitted in ascending order.
